title: Adaptive Entanglement Management in Quantum Multi-Core Architectures
authors: Rajeswari Suance P S, Anubhab Dutta, Ruchika Gupta, John Jose
abstract: Scalable quantum computing architectures increasingly rely on multi-core designs, where qubits are distributed across multiple processing cores interconnected through a quantum Network-on-Chip (NoC). In such systems, inter-core communication is typically realized through entanglement-assisted quantum teleportation, making efficient entanglement generation critical for performance. In this paper, we perform a comparative study of three entanglement management paradigms for multi-core quantum processors: reactive on-demand generation (ODG), proactive continuous pre-generation (CGP), and an adaptive continuous pre-generation approach (ACGP). While ODG generates entanglement only when required, CGP reduces average teleportation latency by pre-generating EPR pairs in the background. To improve upon this, we propose ACGP which dynamically adjusts entanglement generation probabilities based on observed inter-core communication patterns. We evaluate these approaches using an extended SeQUeNCe simulator on mesh-based multi-core architectures on real benchmark circuits. Results show that ACGP significantly reduces average teleportation latency compared to ODG and CGP. Although pre-generation introduces fidelity degradation due to storage time, entanglement purification effectively restores fidelity with minimal impact on latency. These results demonstrate that adaptive entanglement managements can substantially improve communication efficiency in scalable quantum multi-core systems.
summary: This paper analyzes entanglement management strategies for multi-core quantum processors communicating via a Quantum Network-on-Chip. It compares reactive, proactive, and an adaptive approach (ACGP) for generating necessary entangled pairs. The results show that ACGP significantly minimizes communication latency while maintaining high fidelity through background purification.
main_problem: Efficient entanglement generation is critical for performance in multi-core quantum processors because inter-core communication relies on entanglement-assisted quantum teleportation.
main_result: The proposed Adaptive Continuous Pre-Generation (ACGP) strategy significantly reduces average teleportation latency compared to reactive or uniformly proactive methods. Furthermore, entanglement purification can restore fidelity lost during pre-generation with minimal performance penalty.
method: A comparative study evaluating three entanglement management paradigms—On-Demand Generation (ODG), Continuous Pre-Generation (CGP), and ACGP—using simulation on mesh-based architectures.
model_or_system: The system models multi-core quantum processors interconnected via a Quantum Network-on-Chip (NoC). Inter-core communication is simulated using entanglement-assisted quantum teleportation across various mesh topologies ($2	imes1$ to $8	imes8$).
key_observables: Average teleportation latency (ms) and Entanglement Fidelity.
important_parameters: Mesh size ($m 	imes n$), coherence time, and the degree of adaptation in entanglement generation probability.
main_assumptions: The model assumes all-to-all qubit connectivity within each core for simplification; pre-generation introduces fidelity degradation due to storage time.
